**Finding: Compliant** (rule EXCLUSIVITY, no redline proposed)

The Agreement imposes no exclusivity on AP. Clause 1 (Kubient Services) affirmatively disclaims it:

> "Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties."

This is stronger than a mere absence of exclusivity — it is an express carve-out confirming AP may continue to monetise Inventory through competing agents and platforms, so the preferred position is met.

I checked the other "exclusive" hits to rule out exclusivity smuggled elsewhere, and none are restrictive covenants:

- **p0002** — non-exclusive licence of the Auction Platform *to* AP (in our favour; the non-exclusivity here is a Kubient-side concession, not a restraint on us).
- **p0064** — exclusive jurisdiction/venue in New York (forum, not dealing).
- **p0065** — each Party's marks are its own exclusive property (mutual).
- **p0072 / p0073** — entire-agreement and no-third-party-beneficiary boilerplate.

Targeted searches for "sole supplier"/"sole source", requirements-purchase constructions ("shall not procure … from any third party"), "all Inventory", "exclusivity", and "competitor" returned no restrictive language. There is no minimum-volume or all-requirements commitment channelling AP's inventory to Kubient.

One drafting note, flagged for the record rather than as a deviation: the disclaimer sits in the body's Services clause, while the Services themselves are defined by individual Exhibits. If a future Exhibit purports to grant Kubient exclusive access to a category of AP inventory, we would want the body clause to prevail. Worth confirming the order-of-precedence provision resolves conflicts in favour of the main agreement — but that is an Exhibit-precedence point, not an exclusivity breach in the current text.
